requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL support enumerated types.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports enumerated types.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: An enumerated type IS a type that takes only values from a distinct named set of values.
requirements.original: Enumerated types are used to model types that take only a distinct named set of values.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: A distinct named value of an enumerated type IS called an enumerated value.
requirements.original: Such distinct values are called enumerated values.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value SHALL have an identifier.
requirements.original: Each enumerated value shall have an identifier and referencing the values shall only use these identifiers.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: A reference to an enumerated value SHALL only use the identifier of the enumerated value.
requirements.original: Each enumerated value shall have an identifier and referencing the values shall only use these identifiers.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: A reference to an enumerated value IS either in unqualified or in qualified form.
requirements.original: References to enumerated values can occur in two forms: unqualified and qualified.

requirements.subject: ent:unqualified-name
requirements.canonical: The unqualified form of an enumerated value reference consists only of the identifier of the enumerated value.
requirements.original: The unqualified form uses only the identifier of the enumerated value.

requirements.subject: ent:qualified-name
requirements.canonical: The qualified form of an enumerated value reference consists of the enumerated type reference, followed by a dot and the enumerated value identifier.
requirements.original: The qualified form consists of the enumerated type reference, followed by a dot and the enumerated value identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifiers of the enumerated values SHALL be unique within the enumerated type.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values shall be unique within the enumerated type (but do not have to be globally unique) and are consequently visible in the context of the given type only.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifier of an enumerated value NEED NOT be globally unique.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values shall be unique within the enumerated type (but do not have to be globally unique) and are consequently visible in the context of the given type only.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifier of an enumerated value IS visible in the context of its enumerated type only.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values shall be unique within the enumerated type (but do not have to be globally unique) and are consequently visible in the context of the given type only.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: For any instantiation or value reference of an enumerated type, the enumerated type SHALL be implicitly or explicitly identified.
requirements.original: This means that for any instantiation or value reference of an enumerated type, the given type shall be implicitly or explicitly identified.

requirements.subject: ent:type-context
requirements.canonical: If an enumerated type is the type of an element or field of a structured type, the enumerated type IS implicitly referenced via the given element or field at value assignment and instantiation.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: For example, if the enumerated type is an element or field of a user defined structured type, the enumerated type is implicitly referenced via the given element/field (i.e. by the identifier of the field or the position of the value in a value list notation) at value assignment, instantiation, etc. Another example is passing an enumerated value as actual parameter, in which case the type of the corresponding formal parameter establishes the type context needed to make the enumeration value visible.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: When an enumerated value is passed as an actual parameter, the type of the corresponding formal parameter establishes the type context that makes the enumerated value visible.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: For example, if the enumerated type is an element or field of a user defined structured type, the enumerated type is implicitly referenced via the given element/field (i.e. by the identifier of the field or the position of the value in a value list notation) at value assignment, instantiation, etc. Another example is passing an enumerated value as actual parameter, in which case the type of the corresponding formal parameter establishes the type context needed to make the enumeration value visible.

ambiguity.issue: 'enumeration value' is used instead of 'enumerated value'.

requirements.subject: ent:comparison-operator
requirements.canonical: For a comparison operator, if the type of one of the operands is uniquely identified, it IS used as the type context for the other operand.
requirements.original: The third example is the comparison operators: if the type of one of the operands is uniquely identified, it is used as a type context for the other operand (see example 2 below).

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: For the match operation, if the type of the value parameter is not identified, the type of the template parameter establishes the type context.
requirements.original: The fourth example is the match operation, where the type of the template parameter establishes the type context for the operation, if the type of the value parameter is not identified (see example 2 in clause 15.8.2).

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: Within the same module, the identifier of an enumerated value SHALL only be reused within other structured type definitions.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values, within the same module, shall only be reused within other structured type definitions and shall not be used for identifiers of local or global visibility at the same or a lower level of the same branch of the scope hierarchy (see scope hierarchy in clause 5.2).

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: Within the same module, the identifier of an enumerated value SHALL NOT be used for an identifier of local or global visibility at the same or a lower level of the same branch of the scope hierarchy.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values, within the same module, shall only be reused within other structured type definitions and shall not be used for identifiers of local or global visibility at the same or a lower level of the same branch of the scope hierarchy (see scope hierarchy in clause 5.2).

ambiguity.issue: Example 1 declares 'type integer Monday' at module level next to an enumerated type containing Monday and states it does not clash, which contradicts a literal reading of the prohibition (the module level is the same level as the enumerated type definition). Reading 1 (literal text) was chosen.
readings: A definition at the same or lower scope level as the enumerated type definition SHALL NOT reuse an enumerated value identifier (so 'type integer Monday' at module level is an error).

Because enumerated value identifiers are local to their type, only definitions inside the scope of that type context are restricted, and a module-level definition such as 'type integer Monday' is allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value MAY have a user-assigned integer expression or a non-empty list of integer literal values or ranges of integer literal values, given in parentheses after the name of the enumerated value.
requirements.original: Each enumerated value may optionally have a user-assigned integer expression or non-empty list of integer literal values or ranges of integer literal values, which is defined after the name of the enumerated value in parenthesis.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: A user-assigned integer expression of an enumerated value SHALL be statically bound and known at compilation time.
requirements.original: Each user assigned expression shall be statically bound, known in compilation time, and evaluate to an integer value.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: A user-assigned integer expression of an enumerated value SHALL evaluate to an integer value.
requirements.original: Each user assigned expression shall be statically bound, known in compilation time, and evaluate to an integer value.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: Each user-assigned integer value SHALL be distinct within a single enumerated type.
requirements.original: Each user-assigned integer value shall be distinct within a single enumerated type, all ranges of all the values lists shall be disjoint and shall not include any of the used single integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value-list
requirements.canonical: All ranges of all integer value lists of an enumerated type SHALL be disjoint.
requirements.original: Each user-assigned integer value shall be distinct within a single enumerated type, all ranges of all the values lists shall be disjoint and shall not include any of the used single integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value-list
requirements.canonical: A range in an integer value list of an enumerated type SHALL NOT include any of the single integer values used in that enumerated type.
requirements.original: Each user-assigned integer value shall be distinct within a single enumerated type, all ranges of all the values lists shall be disjoint and shall not include any of the used single integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value without an assigned integer value IS associated with an integer number in the textual order of the enumerated values, starting at the left-hand side with zero, in steps of 1, skipping any number occupied by an enumerated value with a manually assigned value or value list.
requirements.original: For each enumerated value without an assigned integer value, the system successively associates an integer number in the textual order of the enumerated values, starting at the left-hand side, beginning with zero, by step 1 and skipping any number occupied by any of the enumerated values with a manually assigned value or value list.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: The integer values associated with enumerated values ARE used to evaluate relational operators on enumerated values.
requirements.original: These values are only used by the system to allow the use of relational operators.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value with an associated integer value list SHALL only be used as a value together with a specific integer value in parentheses after its name.
requirements.original: Enumerated names with an associated value list shall only be used as values together with a specific integer value, which shall be one from the associated list, in parenthesis after the name.

ambiguity.issue: 'enumerated names' is used instead of 'enumerated values' (or their identifiers).

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: The integer value given in parentheses after an enumerated value with an associated integer value list SHALL be one of the values of that list.
requirements.original: Enumerated names with an associated value list shall only be used as values together with a specific integer value, which shall be one from the associated list, in parenthesis after the name.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value with an associated integer value list MAY be used as a template of the enumerated type by adding a list of integer templates and ranges in parentheses after its name.
requirements.original: They can be used as a template of the enumerated type by adding a list of integer template(s) and ranges in parenthesis after the name.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: For an enumerated value with no assigned value or with a specific integer value assigned, the associated integer value SHALL NOT be used directly.
requirements.original: For enumerated values with no value assigned or with a specific integer value assigned, the user shall not directly use associated integer values, but can access them and convert integer values into enumerated values by using the predefined functions enum2int and int2enum (see clauses 16.1.2, C.1.30 and C.1.4).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-enum2int
requirements.canonical: The integer value associated with an enumerated value MAY be accessed using the predefined function `enum2int`, and an integer value MAY be converted into an enumerated value using the predefined function `int2enum`.
requirements.original: For enumerated values with no value assigned or with a specific integer value assigned, the user shall not directly use associated integer values, but can access them and convert integer values into enumerated values by using the predefined functions enum2int and int2enum (see clauses 16.1.2, C.1.30 and C.1.4).

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: The integer value associated with an enumerated value MAY also be used by the system to encode and decode enumerated values.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The integer value also may be used by the system to encode/decode enumerated values.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.condition: the definition is of an imported enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When a module parameter, formal parameter, constant, variable, non-parameterized template or parameterized template whose formal parameters all have default values is defined with an imported enumerated type, the name of that definition SHALL NOT be the same as any of the enumerated values of that type.
requirements.original: When a TTCN-3 module parameter, formal parameter, constant, variable, non-parameterized template or parameterized template with all formal parameters having default values of an imported enumerated type is defined, the name of that definition shall not be the same as any of the enumerated values of that type.

non_requirement.reason: states that encoding is outside the scope of the document, apart from encoding attributes
